newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices static in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices static in thin trade.

text.p: Danish bond prices were becalmed on Monday in trade made thin by an absence of significant foreign indicators, dealers said.
"It looks as if that is how the day will continue, small movements and little activity," a trader said.
At 1050 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.01 point from Friday's close, at 110.93, yielding 6.34 percent, in turnover of one billion crowns.
Its June future fell 0.11 point to 110.50, with five contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.03 point to 89.13.
The crown traded at 3.8080 per mark, weakening from its earlier 3.8070.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one basis point to 60 bp.
Dealers reported foreign interest in the seven percent 2007 government bond, which is in the process of becoming the new benchmark. It traded at 103.41, yielding 6.53 percent.
Bond traders are already using it as a reference point although their professional association still uses the 2006 bond as the benchmark. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom + 45-33-969650
